title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 24-26): Grothendieck is proving the injectivity half of the 'Hom' form of the anabelian conjecture. Let X be a variety and Y an anabelian variety, here an elementary Artin variety (a successive fibration in hyperbolic curves, hence K(pi,1)). Let f, g : X -> Y be dominant morphisms with pi_1(f) = pi_1(g) up to an inner automorphism (equality of outer homomorphisms). The goal is f = g.

The previous page did the abelian step. Through the generalized Jacobian (quasi-Albanese, an extension of an abelian variety by a torus), equality on H_1(-, Z_l) forces maps into a semi-abelian variety G to agree up to a translation. Point (a) there notes that translations of G act trivially on pi_1, so equality cannot be obtained in general.

This page:
(1) Both hypotheses are needed. The anabelian hypothesis on Y is one. Dominance is the other: two constant maps X -> Y to distinct points induce the same (trivial) outer map on pi_1. An earlier attempted counterexample, Y = G x Z with G an elliptic group and Z a finite group, is crossed out.
(2) Claim: an elementary Artin variety Y embeds, via a well-chosen i : Y -> G, into a semi-abelian variety G. Applying the abelian step to i∘f and i∘g gives i∘g = tau_u ∘ (i∘f) for some u in G.
(3) Since f is dominant, Chevalley's theorem gives a nonempty open V ⊂ Y with V ⊂ Im f. Then V + u ⊂ Y, because i(g(x)) = i(f(x)) + u.
(4) Replace X by the open f^{-1}(V). Now f factors as X --f'--> V --j--> Y, with j the inclusion, and g factors as X --f'--> V --j'--> Y, with j' induced by tau_u. So pi_1(f) = pi_1(j)∘pi_1(f') and pi_1(g) = pi_1(j')∘pi_1(f').

The next page uses that the image of pi_1(f') is open in pi_1(V) because f is dominant. This reduces everything to a translation-rigidity statement: if an open U ⊂ Y has U + u ⊂ Y, and the inclusion and the translation induce outer-equal maps on an open subgroup of pi_1(U), then u = 0. Grothendieck then says he does not expect a geometric proof and switches to an arithmetic method.
errors: Notation slip: U first denotes an open of X (with f(U) ⊂ V), then is reused as the open of Y in f' : X -> U, j : U -> Y and pi_1(U). Read U as V in the second half; the next page keeps U for the open of Y.
Order of composition: 'g∘i = tau_u(i∘f)' should read i∘g = tau_u∘(i∘f), as written correctly a few lines earlier.

Gap: the claim that an elementary Artin variety embeds (or at least maps injectively) into a semi-abelian variety is asserted with 'on vérifie'. It is clear for hyperbolic curves via the generalized Jacobian. In dimension >= 2 the quasi-Albanese map can contract fibres when the monodromy coinvariants on fibre H_1 are small, as for Kodaira-type fibrations with an irreducible boundary divisor. Shrinking Y to make it embed into a torus does not obviously preserve the pi_1 hypothesis. The 'bien choisi' in the margin hints that he sensed this. The argument as written is incomplete beyond dimension 1.

ideas.what: Injectivity of Hom(X,Y) -> Hom_out(pi_1 X, pi_1 Y) on dominant morphisms into an anabelian Y; dominance shown necessary via constant maps
ideas.modern_name: Hom-form of the anabelian conjecture (injectivity part, dominant maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Letter to Faltings 1983); later proofs by Mochizuki, Tamagawa and others in the arithmetic setting
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (anabelian section)

ideas.what: Elementary Artin varieties (successive hyperbolic-curve fibrations) as the basic anabelian objects
ideas.modern_name: elementary Artin neighbourhoods / good neighbourhoods (SGA4 XI)
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Artin (SGA 4); anabelian role due to Grothendieck
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings; Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Abelianization via the quasi-Albanese: equality on H_1 forces maps into a semi-abelian variety to differ by a translation
ideas.modern_name: universal property of the generalized Jacobian / quasi-Albanese (Rosenlicht, Serre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht; Serre, 'Groupes algébriques et corps de classes'; Serre, Albanese for open varieties

ideas.what: Reduction of the injectivity problem to translation rigidity: an open U ⊂ Y ⊂ G with U+u ⊂ Y whose inclusion and translate agree outerly on an open subgroup of pi_1(U) forces u = 0
ideas.modern_name: translation rigidity for open subvarieties of semi-abelian varieties

missed.claim: Grothendieck reduces Hom-injectivity for dominant maps, given an embedding into a semi-abelian variety, to a purely geometric translation-rigidity statement. He abandons a geometric proof in favour of an arithmetic one. A geometric proof is plausible over C (e.g. via uniqueness of holomorphic or harmonic maps into hyperbolic targets), but this reduction itself does not appear to be recorded.
missed.quote: on est ramené au cas où f envoie X dans un ouvert V de Y tel que V + u ⊂ Y, et g∘i = τ_u(i∘f)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Injectivity results for dominant maps are known by other means (arithmetic and Kummer-type arguments). The reduction is a modest unpublished detail, and its embedding step is incomplete in dimension >= 2.

deep.surprise_reason: A working draft of the injectivity part of the anabelian Hom-conjecture, which Grothendieck published in conjectural form (Letter to Faltings). The reduction steps are standard (quasi-Albanese, Chevalley). The embedding claim is shaky in higher dimension, and the author himself abandons the geometric route.
transcription_corrections: 'g∘i = τ_u(i∘f)' should be read as i∘g = τ_u(i∘f), consistent with the earlier '(i g) = τ_u(i∘f)'.
In 'f' : X → U' and 'j : U → Y', U denotes the open V of Y introduced just before, not the open of X.
